summary: Scaffolded the Pi-Hub Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript project, renamed the generated template to pi-hub, laid out the layered backend/frontend folder structure from the technical architecture spec, and verified both the frontend build and the Rust backend build (and a live tauri dev launch showing a window titled "Pi-Hub").
completed: Initialized the Tauri 2 project via create-tauri-app with the react-ts template.
Renamed the generated template from tauri-app to pi-hub across package.json, Cargo.toml, and tauri.conf.json; set window title to Pi-Hub at 1280x820 (min 960x640).
Created src-tauri/src/{commands,application,domain,infrastructure,monitoring,platform,storage}/ placeholder modules plus error.rs/state.rs stubs, wired into lib.rs.
Wrote README.md with prerequisites, dev/build commands, project layout, and AIQT usage pointers.
Installed the Rust toolchain (rustup via winget) on the target machine since it was missing, and confirmed MSVC build tools were already present via Visual Studio.
Verified npm run build and cargo build --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml both succeed.
Verified npm run tauri dev launches a live window titled "Pi-Hub" (process pi-hub.exe observed running), then cleanly terminated the dev processes.

validationCommands.summary: tsc + vite build succeeded, produced dist/ bundle.
Rust backend compiled cleanly (2 expected dead_code warnings on placeholder ApplicationError/AppState, silenced with #[allow(dead_code)]).
Live smoke test: window titled "Pi-Hub" opened and pi-hub.exe process was confirmed running, then terminated.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: `npm run tauri dev` launches a blank window on Windows
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: pi-hub.exe process observed running with MainWindowTitle "Pi-Hub".

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Repository layout matches the structure documented in docs/pi-hub-technical-architecture-specification.md section 27
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: src-tauri/src and src folders created matching the documented layered structure.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: cargo build and npm run build both succeed
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Both commands run and completed with exit success; output captured in this session.

notes: Rust was not installed on the target machine; installed via `winget install Rustlang.Rustup` with user confirmation before proceeding.

An earlier `npx create-tauri-app ... -f` run in this session deleted the pre-existing .aiqt/ and docs/ directories as a side effect of force-scaffolding into a non-empty folder; this was caught immediately, and .aiqt project state, the specs, and the design reference files were fully reconstructed from this session's own context/tool-result cache before continuing. No data was lost from the user's perspective, but future work units should avoid re-running scaffolding tools with --force against a non-empty target directory.

Kept src-tauri/src/error.rs (ApplicationError) and state.rs (AppState) as minimal placeholder structs only, matching the documented shapes in the architecture spec section 8.2/22.2 - no business logic was added, deferring that to the M2 work units.
